newsitem.title: USA: MGM Grand reports lower profits.
newsitem.headline: MGM Grand reports lower profits.

text.p: Hotel and casino operator MGM Grand Inc. reported lower fourth quarter earnings Thursday after one-time charges for the opening of its New York, New York Hotel and Casino in Las Vegas.

MGM Grand said it earned $24 million, or 41 cents a share, in the fourth quarter, compared with $31.8 million, or 66 cents a share, a year earlier. Revenues rose to $221.9 million from $206.9 million a year earlier.

The New York, New York hotel and casino, which opened Jan. 3, is 50 percent owned by MGM Grand, which reported a one-time charge of $5.1 million in the quarter related to the preopening costs at the attraction.
Revenues at the flagship MGM Grand hotel and casino, just across the street from New York, New York, rose 4.8 percent due to strong table game play, record room rates and occupancy.
The company said revnues at its MGM Grand Australia rose 61 percent due to unusually high volume and win percentage in baccarat, the company said.
The company said its plans to develop an MGM Grand hotel and casino in Atlantic City, N.J., continue, with about 30 acres of land secured for development.
For the year, earnings were $43.7 million, or 80 cents a share, compared with $46.6 million, or 96 cents a share in 1995. Revenues rose to $861.1 million from $777.8 million a year earlier.
MGM Grand stock was down $1.375 at $38.375 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
